articles.title: Taiwan hopes US arms sale package can be approved soon, president says
articles.summary: Taiwan's President seeks swift US approval for a crucial $14 billion arms sale, reinforcing the island's rejection of unification with China. This move underscores Taiwan's heavy reliance on US military support amidst escalating tensions in the Indo-Pacific. The sale aims to bolster Taiwan's defensive capabilities, highlighting its strategic importance in regional security.

articles.title: Moscow hit by largest Ukrainian attack since start of Russia's full-scale war
articles.summary: Russia's defence ministry reported intercepting nearly 1,000 Ukrainian drones and four cruise missiles nationwide within 24 hours. The statement also mentioned an oil depot being struck. This highlights intense ongoing aerial conflict between Russia and Ukraine, with both sides experiencing significant drone and missile activity, reflecting the dynamic nature of the war.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth warns NATO the US will 'review' its military presence in Europe in wake of 'shameful' lack of Iran war support
articles.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced NATO that the Pentagon will review its force presence in Europe within six months. This strategic move aims to pressure allied nations to significantly increase their defence spending and capabilities. Washington's initiative reflects a broader push for greater burden-sharing within the alliance, crucial amidst evolving geopolitical landscapes and security challenges impacting international defence postures.

articles.title: Submarine repair plans spark shipyard labour dispute in Halifax
articles.summary: Canada's government, Ottawa, is evaluating two Halifax sites for a new submarine maintenance facility. This crucial infrastructure project aims to service Canada's future 12-ship submarine fleet. The facility will ensure operational readiness and long-term support for the naval expansion, highlighting Canada's commitment to strengthening its maritime defence capabilities and national security.

articles.title: In 1962, a French geologist descended into a dark underground cave, but when he emerged more than two months later, he had lost track of time and helped reveal the human body's internal clock
articles.summary: French geologist Michel Siffre conducted a pioneering experiment in the early 1960s. Initially exploring geology, his work evolved into a significant study merging science and human endurance. Siffre endured prolonged underground isolation to research human circadian rhythms and the body's adaptation without external time cues. This groundbreaking research offered crucial insights into our natural biological clock and the psychological impacts of extreme isolation.

articles.title: Bulakovski's team-first attitude leads to NJ's highest individual honor
articles.summary: Ontario coach Rachel Miller is preparing her senior athletes for the 2026 district track and field championships. She conducted individual meetings during an early-week practice, providing personalized attention and motivation. This focused approach aims to enhance each senior athlete's readiness and performance as they gear up for the upcoming competitive events.
